content: For neonates weighing between 2 and less than 4 kilograms, a daily dose of 25 mg was administered. For infants weighing between 4 and less than 8 kilograms, the daily dose was 50 mg. For children weighing more than 8 kilograms, the daily dose was 50 mg. Lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) was given twice daily starting after the first week of life, following a specific dosing regimen: 40/10 mg once daily for neonates weighing between 2 and less than 4 kilograms, and 80/20 mg once daily for infants weighing more than 4 kilograms. This simplified dosing strategy was developed using a World Health Organization (WHO) generic tool, which was based on previously established prophylactic targets for nevirapine (NVP). In recent years, advancements in antiretroviral (ARV) drug formulations for children have led to the availability of improved options, such as dispersible and scored fixed-dose combination tablets, which have largely replaced traditional liquid formulations. These innovations have significantly simplified the delivery of HIV treatment for children in low-income settings. However, the increased variety of formulations across different regimens and weight bands has introduced challenges, including fragmentation of demand, instability in the reliable supply of ARV dosage forms for children, and complications in procurement and supply chain management. Organizations such as the ARV Procurement Working Group and the Global Accelerator for Paediatric Formulations Network provide formulary guidance to programs for selecting optimal ARV drugs for children. These recommendations are based on robust criteria and are regularly updated to align with current WHO guidelines and available products. The most recent revision of the Optimal Formulary was completed in December 2020 and released in April 2021. It includes seven products that deliver recommended firstand second-line regimens across all weight bands for children. Programs are encouraged to procure dosage forms included in the Optimal ARV Formulary for Children. During transitional periods or under special circumstances, such as neonatal treatment, tuberculosis (TB) co-treatment, or third-line antiretroviral therapy (ART), dosage forms listed in the ARV Limited-use Formulary are sufficient to provide appropriate dosing across weight bands for children. There remains an urgent need for better age-appropriate formulations for infants and children living with HIV. Efforts are ongoing to develop additional solid fixed-dose combination formulations, such as ABC/3TC/LPV/r granules, which are in the final stages of approval. The availability of co-formulated darunavir/ritonavir (DRV/r) in a heat-stable fixed-dose combination is also critical for facilitating treatment sequencing and uptake of future secondand third-line regimens for children. Furthermore, the development of formulations containing newer drugs, such as dolutegravir (DTG) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF), is essential for optimizing dosing, sequencing, and harmonization across age groups. WHO continues to work towards simplifying prescribing, dispensing, and dosing guidance while collaborating with pharmaceutical manufacturers and other partners to develop practical recommendations for scaling up ART for children safely and effectively.
